name: Empowering Futures: AKU's Commitment to Literacy

content.title: Empowering Futures: AKU's Commitment to Literacy
content.summary: AKU donates books and shelves to Tanzania's Twiga Primary School, promotes reading culture

media.alt: Empowering Futures: AKU's Commitment to Literacy

content.text: The Aga Khan University (AKU) is deepening its commitment to literacy and community empowerment by helping to establish a new school library at Twiga Primary School in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. This initiative reinforces the University's role in promoting literacy and learning at the community level.

This effort builds on a previous donation of 600 books to the school in 2024, demonstrating the University's belief in competence-based learning and the power of literacy to transform lives. The latest contribution, which includes eight bookshelves and technical support from the AKU Library, will help the school develop a modern, functional library space.
For a school of more than 900 pupils that has long lacked a dedicated reading area, this support will unlock new opportunities for learning and discovery.

During the handover ceremony, Professor Paschal Ruggajo, Associate Dean of the Medical College in Tanzania, emphasized the importance of this work. "The heart of giving back is embedded in AKU's values," he said. "This support comes at a critical time and paves the way for bigger dreams, like developing a proper school library in the near future."

Also present at the ceremony were AKU Tanzania's leadership, Twiga Primary School's Headteacher, Jacquiline Salim Amlungi, two school representatives, and Kessia Kiwia an alumna of AKU, the General Secretary of the Tanzania English Language Teachers Association  (TELTA).
This partnership highlights AKU's belief that a strong foundation in reading and writing is essential for personal growth and community development.
